name: the City Botanic Gardens
title: Ancient Trees in the City Botanic Gardens: 7 to Find
meta_description: Queensland's oldest public garden, planted from the 1860s: the tree that started Australia's macadamia industry, a banyan, a bodhi fig.
intro: Queensland's oldest public garden opened in 1855, and Walter Hill, its first curator, spent the next three decades filling it with plants brought in from across the world; the results are still standing. Seven of the trees we map grow here: the tree that started Australia's whole macadamia industry, a banyan with the finest aerial-root structure of its species in the country, the tallest tree in the gardens at forty-five metres, and a fig said to descend from the tree the Buddha sat under. All are free to walk past, a few minutes apart on paths in the middle of Brisbane's CBD.
